newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bulgaria's inflation to fall sharply-prime ministe.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's inflation to fall sharply-prime ministe.

text.p: Bulgarian Prime Minister Ivan Kostov said on Tuesday he expected a sharp decline in the country's inflation rate over the rest of 1997.

"By the end of the year we expect a sharp decline, so much so that for the rest of the year inflation should not exceed two percentage points per month," he told reporters after meeting the European Union's External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek.
He said that for this month "we expect the figure to be close to zero or very small."

Van den Broek told reporters that the economic and political reform plans unveiled by Kostov on his first overseas visit since being elected had "given a certain sense of optimism" as the Commission finalises advice to EU governments on Bulgaria's application to join the bloc.

Kostov said that he believed the budget plan he has presented will be endorsed by Bulgaria's parliament by the end of this month, and that deals with the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund will be finalised, to allow EU macroeconomic assistance of 250 million ecus to be released. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
